claims.text: RF-based diagnostics can provide information on the oxygen-storage level of a three-way catalyst.
The RF diagnostic can continuously monitor catalyst oxygen-storage state in real time.
The RF signal can be coupled to active control of engine or exhaust parameters.
RF resonant frequency and inverse quality factor are signal parameters relevant to catalyst-state diagnostics.
The RF quality-factor signal is robust below 400 °C.
Resonant frequency is an effective diagnostic at higher operating temperatures.
The integrated sensor and control algorithm will synchronize catalyst oxygen storage with optimal combustion and exhaust conditions.
Oxygen-storage measurements will enable dynamic adjustment of air-fuel ratio or exhaust-gas recirculation.
Dynamic control will maintain the catalyst in an optimal oxygen-storage state.
Maintaining an optimal oxygen-storage state will minimize thermal and redox stresses.
Reduced thermal and redox stresses will suppress catalyst sintering and deactivation.
Suppressing aging and deactivation will enhance catalyst durability and efficiency.
Improved durability and efficiency will permit lower platinum-group-metal loading.
Relative to static operation, RF-based active control will improve catalytic conversion efficiency.
Relative to static operation, RF-based active control will prolong catalyst durability.
The actively controlled catalyst will maintain or improve emission control despite having lower platinum-group-metal loading.
The benefit is expected under driving conditions with moderate-to-high variability in engine load and temperature.
Inaccurate RF state estimation or insufficient control response during extreme transients can eliminate the expected improvements.
The cited RF method uses electromagnetic resonances in a cavity resonator.
The proposed fleet experiment compares RF-controlled vehicles with vehicles using static catalyst operation under identical driving cycles.
